narrative_before: This is a documented CTID emulation of Sandworm (GRU Unit 74455), modelling TTPs from the real 2017 NotPetya campaign and related Exaramel/TeleBots activity. The lab environment has a Linux server 'caladan' (10.0.1.5), domain controller 'arrakis' (10.0.1.4) and Windows user machines 'gammu' (10.0.1.7) and 'quadra' (10.0.1.8). Sandworm logs into caladan over SSH and deploys a P.A.S. PHP webshell, runs discovery, downloads and executes Linux/Exaramel for C2, installs cron/systemd persistence, and exfiltrates /etc/shadow, bash history and SSH keys - cracking credentials for Frank Herbert on gammu. Using those credentials Sandworm uploads Windows/Exaramel to gammu via smbclient and PsExec, keylogs an RDP login, and harvests domain-admin credentials from an active RDP session. It then RDPs from gammu into the domain controller arrakis, uploads NotPetya, and executes it; NotPetya dumps credentials, copies itself to discovered hosts, encrypts files and reboots.

detection_moments.description: Initial access: SSH login to caladan + P.A.S. webshell, Linux/Exaramel downloaded for C2.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Sandworm logs into the Caladan host via SSH and deploys a PHP webshell ... downloads the Linux\\Exaramel ELF executable ... establishes connection to the C2' - Sandworm Operations Flow Steps 11-13

detection_moments.description: Credential exfil + offline cracking; Windows/Exaramel uploaded to gammu via SMB/PsExec, keylogging yields domain-admin creds.
detection_moments.evidence: 'exfiltrates the /etc/shadow, bash history, and SSH keys ... obtains credentials for Frank Herbert on the Gammu host ... uploads Windows/Exaramel to the Gammu host using the smbclient ... obtains domain admin credentials from an active RDP session' - Sandworm Operations Flow Steps 14-17

detection_moments.description: RDP from gammu into DC arrakis; NotPetya uploaded and executed, self-propagating and encrypting/wiping.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Sandworm RDPs into the Arrakis host ... uploads NotPetya to Arrakis ... NotPetya ... copies itself to discovered hosts, and executes itself ... encrypts the files ... reboot' - Sandworm Operations Flow Steps 18-19

attack_path: smbclient upload + PsExec to gammu using cracked Frank Herbert creds - T1021.002 / T1569.002
RDP from gammu into domain controller arrakis with DA creds - T1021.001
NotPetya self-propagation to discovered hosts - T1021.002 / T1486
ambiguities: Documented emulation of the real Sandworm NotPetya campaign (2017); year 2017 set accordingly.
Hostnames (caladan/gammu/arrakis/quadra) and IPs are the plan's lab values (Dune-themed).
DC 'arrakis' disruption set to 5 because the plan detonates NotPetya there (destructive impact on a domain controller); quadra is the self-propagation target.
